name: exp_components
what_changed:
I compared each predicted component with the realised component points on the TRAIN replays. The realised components rebuilt from the history columns and that season's scoring rules add up exactly to the actual points on all 29,177 rows. I made two mechanism-level fixes in model.js (edits marked EDIT(exp_components)). The rest of the model is identical to v1.

(1) Goals-against rate. lc is multiplied by PMC.LCK = 1.05. On TRAIN, realised goals conceded per team-match were higher than lc: 1.06x in 2023-24 (lc 1.565 vs 1.659 goals against) and 1.05x in 2022-23 GW20+. Clean sheets were over-predicted: P(0 conceded) 0.230 predicted vs 0.206 actual, and GK clean-sheet points 0.707 vs 0.619. The lc formula itself is consistent: mean lc equals mu*gr, which equals season-to-date goals per team-match. The gap exists because round-r scoring ran above the season-to-date level in both TRAIN seasons (+4% in 2023-24, +3% in 2022-23). After the fix, 2023-24 P(0) is 0.215 vs 0.206 and goals conceded are calibrated. The change reaches the Monte Carlo through x.lc.

(2) Per-position goal conversion. The finishing shrink target is now each position's goals per xG instead of 1.0: PMC.GF0 = {GK 1, DEF 0.84, MID 1.01, FWD 0.95}, pooled from TRAIN rows with xG. So fin = (g + K_FIN*rho)/(xG + K_FIN). This corrects over-prediction of goals for high-xG defenders and forwards: in the top bins for 2023-24, given the minutes actually played, actual/predicted goals were 0.49 for DEF and 0.87 for FWD. The change reaches the simulation through rates.lamG.

Biases I found but did not ship, because each one made TRAIN MAE worse (all kept in model.js as switches that are off):
- (a) FPL assists per xA is 1.19 for DEF, 1.35 for MID and 2.16 for FWD, but v1 shrinks toward 1. FWD assists are predicted at 0.159 vs 0.259 actual. Fixing it cuts the component calibration error from 0.141 to 0.103, but 2023-24 MAE goes from 1.7659 to 1.7814 and RMSE also rises, because FWD and MID totals are already pushed up by over-predicted minutes.
- (b) The 2022-23 history has xG = 0 (not null) for GW1-15. Up to about GW16 the model then has no clean-sheet or goals-conceded terms, and gr reaches 15. A guard that ignores those rounds fixes the bias (-0.32 to +0.13) and RMSE (2.706 to 2.668), but MAE goes from 1.695 to 1.826.
- (c) Stronger shrinkage of bonus and saves fixes the top-decile over-prediction (e.g. DEF bonus 0.45 predicted vs 0.29 actual), but the effect on MAE is between -0.0002 and +0.0015.
- (d) K_FIN 3 to 12 changed MAE by 0.0005 or less, within noise.

Key metric finding: on 2023-24, a predictor that outputs only the appearance points has MAE 1.603, against 1.766 for v1. MAE rewards something close to median points, not expected points. So changes that make the components mean-correct and add points tend to lose on MAE. Changes that make them mean-correct and remove points win on both MAE and calibration, which is the case for the two shipped fixes.
params: PMC.LCK=1.05 (goals-against rate multiplier; v1 = 1). PMC.GF0={1:1,2:0.84,3:1.01,4:0.95} (finishing shrink target, goals per xG by position; v1 = 1). K_FIN stays 3 and every other PM constant is v1. Off in the shipped config: XG_GUARD=false, AF0=1 (assists/xA; the TRAIN value would be {2:1.19,3:1.35,4:2.16}), PW per-rate prior weights = PRIOR_MIN, KG/KA = K_FIN, GRM=null.
risks:
1) LCK depends on a time effect: scoring rose during both TRAIN seasons, so the season-to-date level lagged. If a season's scoring falls over time, LCK=1.05 over-corrects. Part of its MAE gain is also just "lower predictions win under MAE": LCK=1.09 scores better on MAE than the calibration-based 1.05. I chose 1.05 by calibration, not by MAE.
2) The DEF goals-per-xG ratio is unstable between seasons (0.70 in 2022-23 GW16+, 0.93 in 2023-24). With pooled 0.84, 2023-24 DEF goals go from 4% over to 9% under.
3) 2022-23 is a poor TRAIN season for anything that uses xG, because GW1-15 have xG = 0. Its low v1 MAE is partly an artefact of the model predicting little more than appearance points there.
4) MAE is not a proper metric for expected points. Assist under-prediction, especially for forwards, is real and left unfixed, so the optimizer still undervalues assist-heavy forwards. That fix should be revisited once the minutes layer (over-predicted about 4% in the replay, partly because the replay has no injury news) is calibrated, and together with any exp_minutes change, since they interact.
5) Disclosure: during an early data-format check I printed per-round aggregate goal and xG sums for all three seasons, including 2024-25. Nothing from 2024-25 was used to choose any parameter. The validation MAE was computed once with the frozen configuration; reproduce.sh re-runs that same deterministic evaluation.
6) Validation gain by position: GK 1.978 to 1.948, DEF 1.678 to 1.648, MID 1.578 to 1.576, FWD 2.092 to 2.086. Most of the gain is in GK and DEF.
ship_notes:
Ship it as two constants: copy the PMC block and the edits in pmCtx/pmPlayer from exp_components/model.js. With defaults the code reproduces v1 exactly (checked: max difference 0 on both TRAIN replays).
- LCK multiplies lc inside core(), so clean sheets, goals conceded and the Monte Carlo (oxParams reads x.lc) all stay consistent.
- GF0 enters through lamG = xg90 * finK(...), which the simulation already reads.
- GF0 could be recomputed from complete previous seasons, including 2024-25, before 2025-26 and published as a small JSON.

Paired TRAIN check against v1: 2022-23 -0.0079 MAE (95% CI -0.0098 to -0.0056, round bootstrap, 22 of 34 rounds better); 2023-24 -0.0160 (CI -0.0172 to -0.0149, 35 of 35 rounds better). RMSE also drops on every season: 2.7055 to 2.7043, 2.6809 to 2.6776, and 2.5439 to 2.5415 on validation. Bias falls from 0.039 to 0.002 in 2023-24 and from 0.053 to 0.018 on validation.

The full TRAIN ablation and the per-component predicted-vs-actual tables (v1 and final) are in exp_components/results.json.
